title: Who Convinced Whom? Tracing How LLMs Change Their Minds in Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: arXiv:2610.35930v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Multi-agent debate (MAD) aims to improve language-model decisions through the exchange of arguments, yet agreement after debate need not reflect independent corroboration. We investigate how peer communication influences individual decisions and collective outcomes through behavioral and internal interventions. We introduce MAD Bench, a 2,400-question benchmark spanning knowledge and reasoning, values and moral judgment, and safety and refusal, and evaluate three open-weight models using a round-matched independent-reflection control. Among answer-changing responses, a forced-choice readout before rationale generation matches the eventual answer more often in debate than in reflection (65.4% versus 22.3% on Qwen3.5-9B). Message ablations reveal model-dependent effects of peer answers and reasoning, while attributing identical text to the receiver rather than another agent substantially changes its influence. translated_title: 谁说服了谁？追踪大语言模型在多智能体系统中如何改变主意
translated_abstract: 多智能体辩论（MAD）旨在通过论点交流改进语言模型的决策，然而辩论后达成的一致意见并不一定反映独立的相互印证。我们通过行为和内部干预研究同伴通信如何影响个体决策和集体结果。我们提出了MAD Bench，一个包含2,400个问题的基准，涵盖知识与推理、价值观与道德判断、安全与拒绝三大领域，并采用轮次匹配的独立反思对照条件评估了三个开源权重模型。在改变答案的响应中，在生成理由之前的强制选择读出在辩论场景下比反思场景下更常与最终答案一致（在Qwen3.5-9B上为65.4%对22.3%）。消息消融实验揭示了同伴答案和推理对模型依赖性的影响，而将相同文本归因于接收者本人而非另一个智能体会显著改变该文本的影响力。
tldr: 该论文提出MAD Bench基准，通过行为和内部干预追踪多智能体辩论中大语言模型改变观点的机制，发现辩论后的答案一致性往往源于社会从众效应而非独立验证，且消息的来源归因会显著改变其影响力。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces MAD Bench, a 2,400-question benchmark that uses behavioral and internal interventions to trace how LLMs change their minds in multi-agent debate, revealing that post-debate agreement often reflects social conformity rather than independent corroboration, and that attributing identical text to different sources substantially alters its persuasive influence.
